definitions.explanation: A long, straight section of bamboo used as a pole — for laundry, fishing, vaulting, or supporting plants. Often written {竹竿|たけざお} with kanji.

examples.japanese: {竹|たけ}ざおで{洗濯物|せんたくもの}を{干|ほ}す。
examples.english: To hang laundry on a bamboo pole.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{竹|たけ}ざおの{先|さき}に{釣|つ}り{糸|いと}をつけた。
examples.english: I attached fishing line to the end of a long bamboo pole.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}は、{庭|にわ}に{立|た}てた{竹|たけ}ざおに{布団|ふとん}をかけて{日|ひ}に{当|あ}てたものだ。
examples.english: In the old days, people would drape futons over bamboo poles in the yard to air them in the sun.

notes:
Compound of {竹|たけ} (bamboo) + {竿|さお} (pole, rod). Note the rendaku: さお → ざお. Often written with the kanji {竹竿|たけざお}.

USAGE:
A traditional household and outdoor tool. Familiar Japanese sights: laundry hung on a {竹|たけ}ざお stretched between two posts, the long pole used by the {竹|たけ}ざお{売|う}り (itinerant bamboo-pole seller, whose distinctive call was once common in residential neighborhoods).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {竹|たけ}ざおを{立|た}てる: to set up a bamboo pole
- {竹|たけ}ざおにかける: to hang on a bamboo pole
- {釣|つ}り{用|よう}の{竹|たけ}ざお: a bamboo fishing pole
